newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR says Thailand expelling Karens, voices alarm.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR says Thailand expelling Karens, voices alarm.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency expressed alarm on Friday over the fate of 900 Karen refugees from Burma expelled by Thailand and hundreds of others fleeing violence but blocked from entering the country.
Spokesman Fernando del Mundo said 900 Karens who sought refuge in Thailand were expelled on February 25 and 1,000 others trying to enter the country were blocked at the border.
The Karens are fleeing fighting between Burmese troops and guerrillas of the Karen National Union (KNU), which is fighting for greater autonomy for eastern Karen state.

"We are troubled by this in view of the army offensive. UNHCR is very alarmed by the situation of the Karen refugees at the Thai border with Myanmar. We've raised our concern with Thai officials and we are seeking clarification," del Mundo said.
UNHCR staff are prevented from working in the border camps where some 70,000 Karen refugees have been housed by Thailand since the early 1980s.

A UNHCR mission that visited the provinces of Kanchanaburi and Ratchaburi in the region this week reported that all Karen males over the age of 15 were also being prevented from entering Thailand, del Mundo said.
UNHCR was concerned about the safety of some 2,000 Karen refugees in a border area in Thailand just several miles away from the Myanmar army post, del Mundo added.
The Thai army has denied it is forcibly repatriating Karen refugees arriving across the border from Burma.
The KNU, formed in 1948, has rejected several peace overtures from Burma's military government and remains one of the few ethnic guerrilla groups still fighting Rangoon.
